     "research_note": "A walk from data/frontage/ — not a structure record. WHAT BOUNDED THE RUN, in one place. The treatment is laid on the platted block faces that front THREE east-west streets of the South Division — SOUTH WATER STREET, which is the river bank itself; LAKE STREET one block behind it, both frontages; and RANDOLPH STREET one block behind that, both frontages — between Market Street and State Street. South Water and Lake are the owner's 'at least south of the river or near the river' and the town's trading core in 1835; Randolph is the first tier that is not on the river, added because 'all of the streets should be updated like this' does not stop at the bank. Every face is a committed street centreline offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, so the line a walk lies on is the street network's and not this file's: move a centreline and every board here moves with it. Within that boundary the march decides, face by face and step by step — a stretch carries a walk where the ground is dry committed ground, flat enough for one walking deck, clear of the travelled track and clear of anything already standing on it — and `refused` says which clause refused every stretch that does not. THE SOUTH WATER FRONTAGES STILL COME OUT IN PIECES, and the reason is a finding rather than a fault of this rule: eleven documented buildings on that side were placed against the MODERN kerb rather than against this project's own platted line and stood 4.5 to 8.2 m out past it. Six were reconciled with the plat and their stretch of walk closed; the other five are named one by one in `refused`, with the metres each would have to move and the reason the roof schedule cannot yet absorb the move. WHAT IS STILL OUTSIDE THIS RECORD is the cross streets' own frontages and the West Division across the South Branch — the same rule on more faces, and both refused by a measured triangle count rather than by a promise or by this generator's reach. THE CROSS STREETS ARE NO LONGER REFUSED BY THE CODE: a cross street bounds a block on its EAST and WEST faces, this rule enumerated only NORTH and SOUTH until T-0192, and it enumerates all four now. All seven were built, published and read at the release gate's whole stand set before being left out, and `refused` carries the counts that refused them. What would move it off reconstruction: a Chicago town order on sidewalks of the right date — the corporation legislated wooden walks within a few years of 1835, and an order would give a width and a material at a stroke; a tax, insurance or sale description naming a walk or a fence in front of a named lot; or holding the jail, Green Tree and Sauganash plates as proper source records (T-0075)."

+THE BEST-DOCUMENTED BUILDING IN THIS DATASET, and it is documented from the inside out — which is the opposite of the usual situation here and is worth understanding. The Green Tree survived until 1902, long enough for people who had slept in it to be asked what it was like in print: John Gray, who kept it 1838-41, Edwin O. Gale, who was put up in a chamber 'about 12x12, with two windows 6x8', and F. H. Taylor, who fixed which street the front was on. From them come the room module, the 7 1/2 ft ceilings, the board partitions, the interior whitewash, the dividing hall and its stairway, the bar-room at one end, the attic used for lodging, the gable-end attic window and the low one-storey additions at each end. What none of them gives is an overall dimension, so even here the footprint is a derivation from the room module rather than a measurement. IT ALSO SURVIVED LONG ENOUGH TO BE PHOTOGRAPHED, about 1859, at its original corner — the closest thing to direct visual evidence for any Wolf Point building. Note the caveat carefully, because the version in circulation is wrong: the 1859 plate PREDATES the 1880 move and shows the tavern where it was built, so what stands between it and the scene date is twenty-six years of alteration, not forty-seven years and a move. +#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Hold `frame_tavern_params.front_wall` to the builder it copies (T-3359).
+
+The owner, 2026-11-03, had the 1835 hung signs fixed flat on their fronts, and
+fourteen of them are on frame taverns, whose front elevation nothing could read
+without Blender. `generators/archetypes/frame_tavern_params.front_wall` now states the
+frontage scheme's sash, door, shutter and frontispiece rectangles so
+`tools/generate_business_signboards.py` can stand a board clear of them — but it
+states them as COPIES of `frame_tavern.py`'s literals, because the builder imports
+Blender and the commit gate has none. A copy drifts the day somebody moves a sash in
+the builder and not here, and the board it was keeping off that sash lands on it.
+
+So this reads the builder's SOURCE, finds each literal the reader copies in the line
+that draws it, and fails naming the one that moved. `--self-test` proves the check
+can fail: it re-runs it against a builder source with one sash moved.
+
+  python3 tools/check_tavern_front_reader.py [--self-test]
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "generators"))
+from archetypes import frame_tavern_params as P  # noqa: E402
+from archetypes import frame_dwelling_params as D  # noqa: E402
+from common import openings  # noqa: E402
+
+BUILDER = ROOT / "generators" / "archetypes" / "frame_tavern.py"
+DWELLING = ROOT / "generators" / "archetypes" / "frame_dwelling.py"
+
+
+def _body(src: str, name: str) -> str:
+    m = re.search(rf"^def {name}\(.*?(?=^def |\Z)", src, re.S | re.M)
+    if not m:
+        raise SystemExit(f"FAIL frame_tavern.py has no {name}() — the reader copies it")
+    return m.group(0)
+
+
+def check(src: str, dwelling_src: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
+    fen = _body(src, "_fenestration")
+    fp = _body(src, "_frontispiece")
+    pfe = _body(src, "_pictured_front_entrance")
+    want = [
+        ("_fenestration", fen, f"win_w, win_h, depth = {P.TAVERN_WIN_W_M}, "
+                               f"{P.TAVERN_WIN_H_M}", "the sash size"),
+        ("_fenestration", fen, f"story_h * {P.TAVERN_SILL_FRACTION:.2f}",
+         "the sill at a share of the storey"),
+        ("_fenestration", fen, f"else {P.TAVERN_GROUND_BAYS}", "the ground bays"),
+        ("_fenestration", fen, "i == bays // 2", "the entrance in the centre bay"),
+        ("_fenestration", fen, f"cx - {P.TAVERN_DOOR_HALF_W_M:.1f}, cx + "
+                               f"{P.TAVERN_DOOR_HALF_W_M:.1f}, 0.0, "
+                               f"{P.TAVERN_DOOR_H_M:.1f}", "the door"),
+        ("_fenestration", fen, f"sash_w * {P.TAVERN_SHUTTER_SHARE}", "the shutter leaf"),
+        ("_fenestration", fen, "sash_w / 2 + openings.CASING_W_M + 0.01",
+         "the leaf's hinge line"),
+        ("_fenestration", fen, 'params.front_lower_sash if story == 0 and sgn > 0',
+         "the pictured lower sash, ground front only"),
+        ("_fenestration", fen, 'sash["sill_m"] if sash else z0', "the pictured sash's sill"),
+        ("_pictured_front_entrance", pfe, 'half = g["case_width_m"] / 2',
+         "the pictured entrance case's width"),
+        ("_pictured_front_entrance", pfe, 'outer = g["jamb_outer_width_m"] / 2',
+         "the pictured entrance jambs"),
+        ("_pictured_front_entrance", pfe, 'crown = g["cornice_top_m"]',
+         "the pictured entrance's cornice head"),
+        ("_frontispiece", fp, f"cx - {P.TAVERN_FRONTISPIECE_HALF_W_M:.2f}",
+         "the frontispiece crown's width"),
+        ("_frontispiece", fp, f"{P.TAVERN_FRONTISPIECE_TOP_M:.2f}",
+         "the frontispiece crown's head"),
+    ]
+    bad = []
+    for fn, body, lit, what in want:
+        if lit not in body:

+    if abs(P.TAVERN_HEAD_CAP_M - (openings.HEAD_W_M + openings.CAP_H_M)) > 1e-9:

+                   f"{P.TAVERN_HEAD_CAP_M}")

+    for fn, body, lit, what in (

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""T-3353: a K01 brick rear wing's stone dressings — belts in place of the brick course, and
+quoins at its corners.
+
+1919 Prairie's two rear ranges are quoined at their north-east corners and carry the main
+block's three stone courses across their north walls and stepped-out faces, as the 1919
+programme plate draws them pale against the brick. Held on the committed record:
+
+  * each range registers its quoins, one instance a corner, its courses running from the
+    quoins' foot to the wing's wall top, and limestone stands proud at the corner over that
+    height on both faces;
+  * the garage, which the plate shows no dressings on, is left undressed;
+  * refused: a corner the wing does not have, a quoin through a light, a belt through a light,
+    a belt on a wall the wing has not got, dressings on a frame wing, and stones out of bounds.
+
+    python3 tools/test_k01_wing_dressings.py
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "generators"))
+
+from archetypes import k01_frontage as K1  # noqa: E402
+from archetypes import k01_frontage_params as KP  # noqa: E402
+
+SID = "marshall_field_jr_house_1919_prairie"
+failures = []
+
+
+def check(ok, what):
+    print(("ok   " if ok else "FAIL ") + what)
+    if not ok:
+        failures.append(what)
+
+
+def committed():
+    st = json.loads((ROOT / "data" / "structures" / f"{SID}.json").read_text())
+    return st, st["phases"][-1]
+
+
+def refused(edit, why, says):
+    st, _ = committed()
+    st = copy.deepcopy(st)
+    phase = st["phases"][-1]
+    edit(phase["form"])
+    try:
+        KP.from_phase(phase, st)
+    except KP.ParamError as e:
+        check(says in str(e), f"{why}: refused ({str(e)[:110]}...)")
+        return
+    check(False, f"{why}: refused")
+
+
+st, phase = committed()
+p = KP.from_phase(phase, st)
+a = K1.build(p, SID)
+stone = a.prims["limestone_trim"].pos
+
+for wid in ("middle_range", "rear_range"):
+    w = next(x for x in p.rear_wings if x["id"] == wid)
+    dr = w.get("dressings") or {}
+    q = dr.get("quoins")
+    check(bool(q) and q["corners"] == ("south_front",), f"{wid} names its quoins at its north-east corner")
+    check(set(dr.get("belt_sides", ())) == {"south", "front"} and len(dr.get("belts", ())) == 3,
+          f"{wid} carries three stone belts on its north wall and stepped-out face")
+    c = a.components.get(f"k01.wall.wing.{wid}.quoins")
+    ok = c is not None and len(c["instances"]) == 1
+    check(ok, f"{wid} registers one quoin instance, its corner's")
+    if ok:
+        prm = c["instances"][0]["params"]
+        check(abs(prm["courses"] * prm["course_m"] - (w["top_m"] - q["from_m"])) < 0.01,
+              f"{wid}'s {prm['courses']} courses run from {q['from_m']} m to its wall top {w['top_m']} m")
+    # proud stone at the corner (u1, v0): K01's frame is +X = u, -Z = v
+    u0, u1, v0, v1 = w["rect"]
+    at = [s for s in stone if abs(s[0] - u1) < q["long_m"] + 0.05 and abs(-s[2] - v0) < q["long_m"] + 0.05]
+    ys = sorted(s[1] for s in at)
+    check(bool(ys) and ys[0] <= q["from_m"] + 0.01 and ys[-1] >= w["top_m"] - 0.01,
+          f"{wid}'s corner stands in limestone from {ys[0] if ys else '-'} to {ys[-1] if ys else '-'} m")
+    proud = [s for s in at if -s[2] < v0 - q["proud_m"] + 1e-6] + [s for s in at if s[0] > u1 + q["proud_m"] - 1e-6]
+    check(len(proud) > 0, f"{wid}'s quoins stand proud of both faces at the corner")
+
+garage = next(x for x in p.rear_wings if x["id"] == "garage")
+check("dressings" not in garage, "the garage is undressed")
+
+def wings(f):
+    return {w["id"]: w for w in f["rear_wings"]["value"]}
+
+
+def dress(f):
+    return wings(f)["middle_range"]["dressings"]
+
+
+refused(lambda f: wings(f)["garage"].update(dressings={"quoins": dict(dress(f)["quoins"], corners=["south_front"])}),
+        "a corner on a wall the wing has not got (the garage has no stepped-out face)", "has no south_front corner")
+refused(lambda f: dress(f)["quoins"].update(corners=["south_rear", "south_rear"]), "a corner named twice",
+        "once each")
+refused(lambda f: dress(f)["quoins"].update(long_m=1.6), "a quoin out of bounds", "short < long")
+refused(lambda f: wings(f)["rear_range"]["dressings"]["quoins"].update(long_m=0.9),
+        "a quoin through the rear range's light at s 8.2", "through the light at s 8.2")
+refused(lambda f: dress(f).update(belts=[{"from_m": 3.0, "to_m": 3.2, "proud_m": 0.05}]),
+        "a belt through the lights", "runs through the light")
+refused(lambda f: dress(f).update(belt_sides=["south", "nowhere"]), "a belt on a wall the wing has not got",
+        "name the walls")
+refused(lambda f: dress(f).update(colour="red"), "an unknown dressing", "dressings take")
+refused(lambda f: wings(f)["middle_range"].update(fabric="frame"), "dressings on a frame wing",
+        "brick wing")
+
+print(f"test_k01_wing_dressings: {'all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} FAILED'}")
+sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
